query: Single-phase fcc FeCoNi has high saturation magnetization but a low coercive field, and reported single-phase fcc high-entropy alloys derived from it have coercive fields no greater than 100 Oe in the reported magnetic measurements. What single intervention could overcome this coercivity limitation? Formulate one hypothesis specifying the intervention, its mechanism, the predicted change relative to single-phase fcc FeCoNi or a matched derivative, the relevant compositional, structural, and measurement boundaries, supporting prior evidence, and a controlled experiment with an explicit falsification criterion.

generation.intervention: Pulse electrodeposition to create a dual-phase microstructure with FCC and BCC phases

falsification_experiment.design: Compare the magnetic properties of FeCoNi high-entropy alloy with a dual-phase microstructure created through pulse electrodeposition to those of a single-phase fcc FeCoNi alloy
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the dual-phase microstructure does not exhibit improved soft magnetic properties compared to the single-phase fcc FeCoNi alloy, the hypothesis is falsified

cited_evidence.text: Discovery of advanced soft-magnetic high entropy alloy (HEA) thin films are highly pursued to obtain unidentified functional materials. The figure of merit in current nanocrystalline HEA thin films relies in integration of a simple single-step electrochemical approach with a complex HEA system containing multiple elements with dissimilar crystal structures and large variation of melting points. A new family of Cobalt–Copper–Iron–Nickel–Zinc (Co–Cu–Fe–Ni–Zn) HEA thin films are prepared through pulse electrodeposition in aqueous medium, hosts nanocrystalline features in the range of ~ 5–20 nm having FCC and BCC dual phases. The fabricated Co–Cu–Fe–Ni–Zn HEA thin films exhibited high saturation magnetization value of ~ 82 emu/g, relatively low coercivity value of 19.5 Oe and remanent magnetization of 1.17%. Irrespective of the alloying of diamagnetic Zn and Cu with ferromagnetic Fe, Co, Ni elements, the HEA thin film has resulted in relatively high saturation magnetization which can provide useful insights for its potential unexplored applications.

Co–Cu–Fe–Ni–Zn nanocrystalline dual phase HEA thin films have been fabricated by pulse electrodeposition in a single step. Crystallinity, required compositional range of elements and phases in HEA thin films have been derived by the application of pulse in the electrodeposition. Where, pulse enabled the deposits with homogeneous distribution and composition throughout the film with dual phase of FCC and BCC having a nanocrystalline grain size ranging between ~ 5 and 20 nm. Impressive soft magnetic behaviour qualifies these HEA thin films as a novel functional material for several magnetic applications, where these HEAs are expected to have better corrosion/oxidation resistance over the conventional magnetic materials due to the presence of oxidation resistant elements in the existing alloy.
